:::{#exm-chebyshev-auto}
#### How loose is Chebyshev's bound for car horsepower?

Take the 392 horsepower values in the Auto data
described in @exm-clt-auto as the whole population,
and draw one car at random.
For each $k$, the code below counts the share of cars whose horsepower
is at least $k$ standard deviations from the mean,
and sets it beside the bound $1/k^2$ from @thm-chebyshev.

```{r}
#| label: chebyshev-auto
#| code-fold: false
hp <- read.csv("data/auto.csv")$horsepower
mu <- mean(hp)
sigma <- sqrt(mean((hp - mu)^2))

k <- c(1.5, 2, 3)
share_beyond <- sapply(k, function(kk) mean(abs(hp - mu) >= kk * sigma))
data.frame(k = k, share_of_cars = share_beyond, chebyshev_bound = 1 / k^2)
```

```{r}
#| include: false
# The claims the prose makes: the bound holds at every k, and it is
# at least twice the observed share at k = 2 and k = 3.
stopifnot(
  all(share_beyond <= 1 / k^2),
  share_beyond[2] * 2 <= 1 / k[2]^2,
  share_beyond[3] * 2 <= 1 / k[3]^2
)
```

The bound holds at every $k$, as @thm-chebyshev guarantees.
At $k = 2$ the share of cars is
`{r} round(100 * share_beyond[2], 1)`%,
against a bound of `{r} round(100 / k[2]^2)`%,
and at $k = 3$ it is `{r} round(100 * share_beyond[3], 1)`%
against `{r} round(100 / k[3]^2, 1)`%.
The bound is loose because it must hold for every distribution with this mean and variance.

:::
